extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art history, architects, and scholars of Renaissance art and architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Normative and descriptive criteria, as given in a biographical/art-historical account (Vasari), for judging and producing Renaissance painting, sculpture, and architecture — focusing on proportion, materials, construction methods, harmony, ornament, inventiveness, and personal virtues. Emphasizes practical engineering, classical canons, and patron satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fortification completeness and defensive provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Giuliano fortified Castellina with good walls and mills, both within and without, and furnished it with everything else necessary for the defence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defensive works should include comprehensive provisions (walls, mills, bastions, works for artillery) and be fully furnished to serve their military purpose; completeness and attention to all necessary elements are a mark of a successful fortification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe and knowledgeable artillery handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The artillery-men stood at a great distance from their pieces, handling, loading, and discharging them with much timidity... he so contrived that from that time onwards the artillery did harm to no one, whereas it had previously killed many of them, since they had not had judgment and knowledge enough to avoid suffering injury from the recoil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective military engineering requires technical knowledge and safe procedures: proper handling techniques and training to avoid injuries from recoil are essential; ignorance is an anti-pattern that causes harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classical capital proportions and borrowing from antiquity
rubrics_metrics.description: Placing capitals on the columns with volutes curving downwards to the collarino... and making, below the ovoli and the fusarole, a frieze, one-third in height of the diameter of the column. This capital was copied from a very ancient one of marble... prized for its beauty and variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt and study ancient models for proportion and ornament; precise proportional rules (e.g., frieze height relative to column diameter) are important—copying exemplary ancient examples is praised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of models to persuade patrons and communicate difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Giuliano made a model... so that he might show from the model itself the difficulties that he had triumphed over in making it... having presented the work, was received with honour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical models are valuable tools to demonstrate constructability, explain complex solutions to patrons, and secure commissions; they serve as concrete proof of design judgment and overcome scepticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventiveness that pleases the patron
rubrics_metrics.description: Giuliano made it so completely different in form from the others, and so much to Lorenzo's fancy, that he began straightway to have it carried into execution, as the best of all the models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation and a distinctive form that fits the patron's taste are positive attributes; originality that satisfies the client's expectations can determine selection and execution of a design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof-of-concept construction to establish feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Giuliano, who was building a house for himself in Florence, made a ceiling for his hall according to the design of the other, in order to convince the mind of that Magnificent Prince; and Lorenzo therefore gave orders for the ceiling at the Poggio to be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructing a smaller-scale or demonstrative version of a proposed structural element is an effective way to prove feasibility and gain approval for larger works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate materials and mixtures for structural stability
rubrics_metrics.description: To the end that this structure, besides beauty of form, might be firm, solid, stable, and well bound in the stonework, he sent to Rome for pozzolana; nor was any lime used that was not mixed with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and use proper materials (e.g., pozzolana-lime mixtures) to achieve lasting, stable masonry; material choice and correct mixing are essential construction standards for durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting programmatic and functional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorenzo wished to build a convent capable of holding a hundred friars... models were made by many architects, and in the end that of Giuliano was put into execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs must satisfy explicit functional requirements (capacity, program) of the commission; successful proposals meet the stated needs of the institution or patron.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-arranged and balanced ornamentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A vast number of beautiful adornments in it, so well arranged and distributed, and all accommodated in their places with art and grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ornament should be plentiful yet well-composed and harmoniously distributed; balance and grace in decorative elements mark superior design rather than arbitrary richness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to classical canons and improvement of orders
rubrics_metrics.description: They bequeathed to the art of architecture methods that gave the Tuscan Order of building better form than any other architect had yet achieved, and the Doric Order they enriched with better measures and proportions than their predecessors, following the rules and canons of Vitruvius.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect classical rules (e.g., Vitruvius) while seeking to refine and improve proportions of established orders; canonical knowledge combined with thoughtful refinement is praised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative construction techniques (vault casting/ready-carved materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Giuliano brought from Rome the method of casting vaults with such materials as made them ready carved; examples of which may be seen in a room in his own house, and in the vaulting of the Great Hall at Poggio a Cajano.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovations in construction methods that yield efficient, high-quality results (e.g., ready-carved vault elements) are notable achievements; practical technical innovation is a positive criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of perspective and pictorial composition
rubrics_metrics.description: A temple drawn in perspective with such loving care, that it is a marvellous thing to see the difficulties that he was for ever seeking out in this branch of his profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate, careful use of perspective in composition is a mark of excellence in painting; seeking out and solving pictorial difficulties is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical proficiency through imitation and development
rubrics_metrics.description: Raffaello, studying the manner of Pietro, imitated it in every respect so closely, that his copies could not be distinguished from his master's originals... and one may recognize the excellence of Raffaello increasing and growing in refinement, and surpassing the manner of Pietro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early technical mastery often proceeds via close imitation of a master; the capacity to replicate and then refine or surpass the master's manner is an indicator of high skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal virtues, conduct, and reputation of the artist
rubrics_metrics.description: Endowed by nature with modesty and goodness... the beautiful adornment of courtesy and grace... industry, beauty, modesty, and excellence of character... whom men regarded as agreeable and pleasant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral qualities and conduct (modesty, courtesy, industry) are presented as integral to an artist's esteem and success; character affects reputation and patronage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony with existing fabric when extending buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: He made models for the aisles of the Madonna delle Lacrime, although that work was very badly conceived, because it is out of harmony with the original part of the building, and the arches at the ends are not in true line with the centre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additions or restorations must respect the character, harmony, and alignment of the original structure; lack of correspondence in scale, proportion, or axial alignment is a design failing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, situation-aware engineering solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: They constructed a bridge, which was a very ingenious piece of work, since, besides the fact that, rising or falling with the water, and being well bound with chains, it stood safe and sound against floods, it carried out the desires of the commissaries... that the Pisans... were forced to come to terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineering solutions should respond to site conditions and operational constraints (e.g. tidal/flooding rivers); ingenuity that solves tactical or logistical problems is highly valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculptural technical mastery (single-block carving)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Madonna of marble, with the Child in her arms, and lying in the lap of S. Anne, ... with the figures carved in the round out of one single block, was held... to be very beautiful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to execute complex sculptural groups carved wholly from a single block is a demonstration of superior technical mastery and is highly esteemed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civic ornamentation and public benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorenzo, in order to benefit the commonwealth and adorn the State, and at the same time to leave behind him some splendid monument... wished to execute the fortification of the Poggio Imperiale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that serve public benefit and enhance the civic fabric are particularly laudable; architecture as civic ornament and public utility is an important evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability and resilience in times of conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Some completed parts did not long remain standing, because in 1530, on account of the siege of Florence, it was destroyed... and many works were broken to pieces on the arrival of the French...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider durability and resilience of works under political/military upheaval; proper foundations, defences, and construction methods contribute to longevity despite conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to patrons and courtly tastes
rubrics_metrics.description: When he had presented the model to him, on the part of the Magnificent Lorenzo, the Duke was filled with astonishment... The gift was so welcome and acceptable to the King, that he rewarded Giuliano liberally and gave him infinite praise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding and catering to the tastes and expectations of patrons and courts (presentation, courtesy, appropriate gifts) affect an artist/architect's success and recognition.
